rows.03:8aac:
The ritual was held in the gym, at night.
Tadokoro and the ghost of the former member laid out the ritual ingredients on the floor beneath the basketball hoop.
Tadokoro had prepared three ingredients.
As for the last one...{p}
rows.03:8b5c:
"Don't worry.
I've got it all ready.
You don't need to worry about a thing."
That's what the ghost said.
And it was the ghost who chanted the spell to summon the demon.
"Rechirayoyaieumimuchi... Show thyself.
O demon who feeds upon memories.
Come forth to me☆"{p}
rows.03:8c58:
...Sure enough, the demon appeared.
Tadokoro poured his heart out to it, telling it everything he wanted.
The demon granted Tadokoro's wish.
And then...{p}
rows.03:8d18:
Tadokoro collapsed to the floor.
"My head, ah... my head...☆"
Clutching his head, Tadokoro writhed in agony.
"...Tadokoro.
Thank you for providing the last ingredient.
You've met the same fate I did.
I don't want to go to the spirit world alone, you see.
Come on, let's go together..."
...It was the ghost's voice.
Then, with a nasty smile on its face, the ghost vanished into the darkness.{p}
rows.03:8e8c:
Do you know what that last ingredient was?
...I'll tell you.
It was a human skull, that's what.
The demon tore the skull right out of Tadokoro, and he died.
That's why, they say, there was no skull among his remains.
The ghost had died the same way, with his skull torn out.
When he was alive, the demon tricked him into trying the ritual with three ingredients, and it killed him.
That's what it really meant when they said that member died in an accident.{p}
rows.03:9024:
Oh yeah, about the basketball guys and Kawaguchi.
Just like the deal with the demon said, they've completely forgotten all the nasty stuff about Tadokoro.
So now they're grieving over his death, and supposedly they've put his picture up in the club room.
If you put up a picture like that, isn't something bound to happen all over again?{p}
rows.03:9128:
...{a}, you play sports, right?
Which club are you in?
If you're in the basketball club... watch yourself.
They say the notebook about the demon ritual is still in the boys' basketball club room, even now.
Make sure you don't end up as an ingredient in the ritual...
Well then, let's hear the next one's story...{p}
rows.03:93b8: That's right, that night he just didn't go, for no particular reason.{p}
rows.03:93ec:
But the next day, he regretted it and wished he'd gone after all.
The only one who could understand how he felt now was the upperclassman.
He wanted to go see the upperclassman again... no, as many times as he could.
That's what he thought.{p}
rows.03:94ac: After that, for a while, the two of them kept up their late-night meetings almost every day.{p}
rows.03:94f0:
That's right, something happened to come up and he couldn't go.
He was really bitter about it, too.{p}
rows.03:9550: The next day, he filled that notebook with everything: his passion for basketball, how he was feeling at the time, all of it.{p}
rows.03:95b4:
Then the upperclassman gave him all sorts of advice about what he'd written in the notebook.
Tadokoro was deeply moved.
My upperclassman understands everything about me, and really thinks things through for my sake...
That's what he thought.
From then on, no matter what else he had to do, Tadokoro kept going back to see the upperclassman.{p}
rows.03:9718:
I see, you don't have one.
...The guy who took the pictures of Tadokoro getting beaten up by the track team guys was supposedly named {a}.
Might just be a coincidence, but you've got a bit of his look about you, so I figured you two might be siblings.
So you don't have an older brother...
...You're not lying to me, are you?
Well, whatever.{p}
rows.03:9820:
If you really do have an older brother...
You should ask him about it sometime.{p}
rows.03:9884:
He rounded up some new members from who knows where and formed his very own basketball team.
"My teammates all understand me. They're the best friends anyone could have.
They're worlds apart from those track team guys and the basketball club here."
That's what he said, they say, bragging about it nonstop.
With his eyes glittering.
Not that anybody actually took what he said seriously...{p}
rows.03:9a04:
Tadokoro was found dead under the basketball hoop in the gym.
He must have snuck in during the night to practice.
They say there were tons of basketballs lying around him.
Everyone knew Tadokoro had made his own private basketball team, after all.{p}
rows.03:9bf0:
...And ever since then.
They say you can sometimes hear the sound of a ball being bounced in the gym.
Maybe Tadokoro's still in there practicing, even now?
Together with his teammates.
Not that I've seen it myself yet, though.{p}
rows.03:9cc0:
Hey, {a}.
Since you're doing the interview anyway, how about we go take a look at the gym right now?
It's getting pretty dark out, too.
What do you say?{p}We might get to meet Tadokoro's ghost.
rows.03:9d6c:
That's what I like to hear.
All right then, let's head to the gym.{p}
rows.03:9dcc:
Man, this gives me a bad feeling.
This hallway...
It's awfully quiet, isn't it?
Did everybody go home already?
Still, this school sure is huge.
Even getting to the gym is a pain.{p}
rows.03:9e80:
Well, whatever, we're here.
Hey, {a}.
You can still turn back now.
What'll it be?{p}Are you going in?
rows.03:9ef4:
...Don't come crying to me later.
All right, I'm opening it.{p}
rows.03:9f38:
I can't really see a thing.
Somebody turn on the lights.{p}
rows.03:9fa8:
Huh?
What the hell, where'd everybody else go?
"Oh, um..."
I looked around.
There was nobody in the gym but Shindo and me.{p}
rows.03:a098:
"...{a}.
Were you the one who turned on the lights?"
Shindo was frowning.
I hadn't turned on any lights.
When I shook my head, Shindo lowered his voice.
"I didn't turn them on either.
Then who did?"{p}
rows.03:a1e8: Just then, the entrance doors suddenly slammed shut.
rows.03:a284:
"Looks like we've gotten ourselves into a real mess..."
There was no sign of anyone else in the gym.
But was that really true?
Maybe someone was hiding and playing a prank on us...{p}
rows.03:a328:
...What's that?
I could hear footsteps.
Squeak, squeak... footsteps on the gym floor.
They were coming closer and closer.
No...
But there's nobody else here...
The footsteps stopped dead, right beside us.{p}
rows.03:a40c:
"Tadokoro?"
Shindo suddenly said something like that.
No way.
Can Shindo see him?
Is he talking to this Tadokoro person?
"What's that... huh? You're giving it to me?"
Shindo held out his hand.
It looked like he was taking something.
But I couldn't see Tadokoro, or whatever it was Shindo had taken.
"Um, Shindo..."
"Shh."
Shindo was staring intently at whatever he'd been given.
Footsteps echoed nearby again.
Tadokoro, who had been beside us, seemed to have started walking.
Before long, the footsteps faded into the distance.{p}
rows.03:a5f8:
"Hey, what's going on?"
With that voice, the entrance doors suddenly flew open.
As if I'd woken from a dream, all the tension drained out of me at once.
Everyone who'd been outside came in.{p}
rows.03:a6a8:
"That gave me such a fright!
The doors just slammed shut all of a sudden!
Hey, are you all right?"
"Honestly, that was dangerous.
A girl shouldn't be left all alone with a guy in a place like a gym.
I thought my heart was going to stop.
You're cute, after all, {b}."
"Heh heh heh...
Did you get to meet this Tadokoro, or whatever his name was?
Oh dear, you're drenched in sweat."
Everyone was saying all sorts of things at once.
"Let's go back to the club room..."
That was all I could manage to say.{p}
rows.03:a850:
"Wait a moment.
Are you leaving him behind?"
Iwashita pointed.
Oh, that's right.
Shindo was still inside the gym.{p}
rows.03:a8e4:
"Um, Shin..."
Shindo was looking at something and muttering to himself.
...Oh no, what's happened to him?
Something about him makes it hard to even speak to him.{p}
rows.03:a980:
"Well, why not?
Let's just leave him here."
Iwashita said something terribly cold.
"But..."
"His story is finished.
You have other work to do, don't you?"{p}
rows.03:aa3c: ...What should I do?{p}Shindo was still looking at what he held in his hands, still muttering.
rows.03:aaa0: Maybe I have no choice but to leave him.{p}
rows.03:aac8: I left the gym together with everyone else.{p}
rows.03:ab1c:
Back in the club room, just as I'd caught my breath, Shindo came back.
...Thank goodness.
Still, what was that back there?
Is Shindo really all right?
At a glance, he doesn't seem to have changed much...
And he doesn't have that dazed look in his eyes like before.
Well, there's no use dwelling on it.
I have to hear the next story.
Now, whose story should I hear next...?{p}
rows.03:ac90:
What, you're no fun.
...Well, if you don't want to, fine.{p}
rows.03:accc:
Oh yeah, {a}, you play sports, right?
If you're in the basketball club... watch yourself.
Don't let Tadokoro recruit you.
Looks like it doesn't matter to him whether you're a guy or a girl.
Well then, let's hear the next one's story...{p}
rows.03:ae24:
Well, fine, you're the one writing the article.
It's not my place to butt in.
Come on, let's head back to the club room.
...Guess I'll pin my hopes on the next one's story.{p}
rows.03:aeac:
"I'll go get him."
With that, I went over to Shindo.
"Shindo."
Even when I spoke to him, there was still no answer.
What should I do...?{p}
rows.03:af3c:
"We'll go on ahead."
One of them said it, and everyone started to leave.
No, I can't stay in a place like this a moment longer.
"Please wait!"{p}
rows.03:afc4:
I went after everyone.
Feeling guilty the whole time...{p}

03:a6a8: three unnamed speakers (likely Fukuzawa, Kazama, Iwashita); not named in English, as in the source.
